title: SentinelFlow shared primitives, v1
description: Types reused across every SentinelFlow contract. Defined once so that a change to how money or an identifier is represented is a single edit rather than a search. Binding rules live in ADR-0007.

uuid.description: A UUIDv7. Time-ordered so inserts append to an index rather than scattering across it. See ADR-0007.

timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, ISO 8601 with an explicit offset. Stored as timestamptz. See ADR-0007.

money.description: A decimal amount as a STRING, never a JSON number. JSON.parse produces a double, so a JSON number is silently rounded by every JavaScript consumer before application code sees it. Scale is at most 4 to match NUMERIC(19,4). Always paired with a currency. See ADR-0007.

currency.description: ISO 4217 alphabetic code. Never implicit: an amount without a currency is not money, it is a number that looks like money.

amount.description: A monetary value. The only shape in which an amount ever appears in a SentinelFlow contract.

accountReference.description: Synthetic, human-readable account handle. Unique, but never a primary or foreign key.

riskBand.description: The banding a final score falls into. Ordered least to most severe.

score.description: A risk score from 0 to 100 inclusive. A JSON number is correct here: this is a computed measure, not money, and a rounding difference in the last place changes nothing a decision depends on.

alertStatus.description: Alert lifecycle state. Valid transitions are defined by the API, not by this enum - listing a state here does not make every transition into it legal.

reasonCode.description: One contributing factor behind a score, with how much it contributed. Reason codes are what make an assessment explainable to an analyst who has to defend a decision later.

code.description: Stable machine-readable identifier. Never renamed once emitted - a renamed code silently breaks every historical query.

contribution.description:
How much this factor pushed the score, on the scale its `source` uses.

For a `RULE` it is the configured weight on the 0-to-100 scale, and the rule reasons sum to `ruleScore` - which is the whole appeal of a ruleset: an analyst can add them up and get the number.

For a `MODEL` it is the estimator's own decomposition, signed, on its own scale. It explains the ranking, deliberately does not sum to anything, and is only comparable within one `modelVersion` - the same statement `ReasonContribution` makes in the scoring contract. That is why this field carries no numeric bound: a log-odds contribution has no natural ceiling, and clamping one to fit a range would change a number an analyst reads without saying so.

source.description: Whether this came from a deterministic rule or from the model.

version.description: A model, feature, or policy version. Semantic-version-like, compared as an opaque string rather than parsed.
